name: Upstash
tagline: Serverless, per-request-priced Redis with an HTTP API built for edge and serverless functions.
description: Upstash runs a Redis-compatible database as a serverless service: you pay per command (or a flat plan), idle databases cost nothing, and an HTTP/REST API lets Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge and AWS Lambda use it without persistent TCP connections. Data is persisted to disk and can be replicated globally with reads served from the nearest region. The same company offers QStash (HTTP message queue), Vector, Search and Workflow products. It suits low-to-moderate traffic apps and edge functions; at sustained high throughput a fixed-price plan or self-managed cache usually wins.

pricing.notes: Free tier with 256 MB and 500K commands/month; fixed plans from $10/month with unlimited commands.

scale.notes: Global databases replicate to multiple read regions; fixed plans go up to hundreds of GB.

strengths: Scale-to-zero pricing: idle databases are free
HTTP API works from edge runtimes that cannot open TCP sockets
Global read replicas close to edge functions
Generous free tier and Vercel/Cloudflare integrations
weaknesses: Per-command pricing gets expensive at sustained high throughput
HTTP round trips add latency versus a co-located cache
Not every Redis command or module is supported
Proprietary service with no self-hosted option
useCases: Rate limiting and caching in edge and serverless functions
Session storage for Next.js and Vercel apps
Side projects and low-traffic production apps
notIdealFor: Workloads needing self-hosting or VPC-only access
